replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset while retaining as much variability as possible. The steps involved in performing PCA include standardizing the data, computing the covariance matrix, calculating the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix, sorting the eigenvalues in descending order, and selecting the top k eigenvalues and their corresponding eigenvectors to form a feature vector. Finally, you can transform the original dataset into a new subspace using the selected feature vectors. As for the mathematics involved in PCA, it can be quite complex and may require a strong background in linear algebra and statistics. However, there are many software tools and libraries available that can perform PCA for you, so you don't necessarily need to understand the underlying mathematics to use it.
